thread.title: Dow, S&P 500 close slightly higher, but tech weakness leads to overall lackluster action

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Dow, S&P 500 close slightly higher, but tech weakness leads to overall lackluster action
text:
U.S. stocks ended the session slightly higher Wednesday as gains in consumer-staples XLU, -0.09% but weakness in the technology and internet-related sector capped more significant advances, even as Wall Street digested midday reports that the U.S. and China may enter a fresh round of trade negotiations. The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.11% finished up 0.1% at 25,999, the S&P 500 gained less than 0.1% at 2,889, supported by a 1.3% rise in the consumer-staples sector. However, a 0.8% decline in financials XLF, -0.92% and a 0.5% slide in tech names capped the broad-market benchmark's climb. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -0.23% fell 0.2% at 7,954, as declines in the shares of chip makers weighed on the tech sector. A popular gauge of chip makers, the iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF SOXX, -1.16% ended down 1.1%, led by declines in shares of Micron Technology Inc. MU, -4.27% Meanwhile, shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.24% declined 1.2%, even as the gadget maker rolled out updates to its iPhones and Apple Watches. On the trade front, the U.S. has reached out to China for follow-up talks after negotiations last month concluded without results, according to The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday. In the latest economic data, the wholesale cost of U.S. goods and services fell in August for the first time in a year and a half as the recent upturn in inflation appeared to ease.The U.S. economy grew at a "moderate pace" even though there were pockets of weaker activity in certain districts, according to the latest Beige Book released.
See Full Story Stock market logs mostly muted gain as tech lags in choppy session U.S. stocks close mostly higher on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and the Dow bouncing back from lows. However, the Nasdaq’s effort to build on its recent gains hit a wall.
